optionReasons.saa-ini-050:option:0: Infinite synchronous restraints secure resources, degrade payment and overload recovery service.
optionReasons.saa-ini-050:option:1: Funding services AUMENTA the coupling: a failure anywhere knocks down the set.
optionReasons.saa-ini-050:option:2: Greater instance does not change the fragility of synchronous coupling: any drop in emission continues to bring down payments.

finalJustifications: Because the queue unplugs the services: the payment goes public and continues to work, and the issue processes the accumulated messages when it recovers.
Because SQS detects the emission service drop and automatically resets it, restoring the original synchronous flow.
Because SQS converts synchronous calls into faster batch requests, reducing payment response time.
Because the queue prioritizes outstanding tax bills, ensuring issuance in less than a second even during unavailability.

finalJustifications: Because Security Group is a stateful firewall at the instance level: the response of a permitted traffic is automatically released.
Because Security Group isolates processes within the instance itself, blocking traffic between local applications.
Because Security Group apply explicit denial rules (deny) evaluated in numerical order, such as NACLs of the subnet.
Because Security Group filter traffic only at the exit of the VPC, leaving the entrance on behalf of Internet Gateway.

optionReasons.saa-ini-290:option:0: The Kinesis Data Streams ingests in real time, but requires you to build and operate the consumer application (EC2/KCL) — It's MAIS operational effort, not less.
optionReasons.saa-ini-290:option:2: SQS is point-to-point message queue — is not streaming service and has no native delivery on S3.
optionReasons.saa-ini-290:option:3: The Glue streaming process data with Spark and requires writing and maintaining a job — it is not a simple and managed delivery service at S3.

finalJustifications: Because Firehose is a service of ENTREGA totally managed: receives the stream, makes buffer (~60(s) and automatically deposit in S3, no servers or consumer code.
Because Firehose offers latency on delivery, the smallest of the whole family Kinesis — ideal for real-time clicks.
Because Firehose stores data permanently within the service itself, dispensing the S3 as a persistence layer of clickstream.
Because Firehose doesn't charge for stream intake, only for final storage — the lowest operating cost of the family Kinesis.

optionReasons.saa-ini-291:option:0: No. SQS each message is consumed by ONE consumer and removed from the queue — there are no multiple readers independent of the same stream or replay.
optionReasons.saa-ini-291:option:1: The AWS Batch performs batch computing jobs — does not continuously ingest real-time events.
optionReasons.saa-ini-291:option:3: The EventBridge Scheduler triggers tasks at scheduled times — it is not streaming intake service.

finalJustifications: Because Kinesis Data Streams ingests events with subsequent latency and allows several consumers to read the same stream independently, with replay within retention.
Because Kinesis Data Streams delivers each event to exactly one consumer, ensuring the exclusivity that sustains the subsequent latency.
Because Kinesis Data Streams is a row FIFO managed built on the SQS, inheriting the strict ordination and fan-out of the default rows.
Because Kinesis Data Streams records events directly on S3 without consumers, and applications read files deposited in real time.

optionReasons.saa-ini-137:option:1: Authentication IAM control QUEM You can call API — does not reduce invocations or latency of repeated requests.
optionReasons.saa-ini-137:option:2: Increasing the timeout only allows longer executions; each request continues to invoke the Lambda and consulting the bank.
optionReasons.saa-ini-137:option:3: HTTP APIs are cheaper and lighter, but DO NOT have built-in cache — repeated invocations would continue to happen.

finalJustifications: Because the stage cache keeps the answer for a TTL configurable and responds to identical cache requests directly, without invoking the Lambda nor consult the bank.
Because the cache of API Gateway moves function Lambda to the edge, executing it in the edge locations of the CloudFront at each identical request.
Because the cache preheats the database responses asynchronously, consulting it before the requests reach the endpoint.
Because the cache elevates the maximum timeout integration of Lambda, allowing repeated consultations to end before expiry.

optionReasons.saa-ini-143:option:0: The S3 Transfer Acceleration accelerates uploads to S3 by the edge of the CloudFront — does not affect the network ENTRE cases EC2.
optionReasons.saa-ini-143:option:2: Public sub-network only changes router to the internet — no improvement PPS, latency or jitter between instances.
optionReasons.saa-ini-143:option:3: Volume size EBS affects storage (IOPS/throughput of disk), not network performance.

finalJustifications: Because Enhanced Networking with the driver ENA use SR-IOV, delivering much higher rate of packages per second, lower latency and minimum jitter in supported instances.
Because ENA compresses network packages into hardware before shipment, reducing traffic volume and raising the rate of PPS between instances.
Because Enhanced Networking establishes a VPN dedicated between the clusters, with low latency tunnels and controlled jitter.
Because ENA transfers the processing of packages to a managed intermediate buffer, releasing the CPU of the application instance.

optionReasons.saa-ini-148:option:0: Standard Workflows have lower rate limits and charge by state transition — expensive and limited to millions of short executions per day.
optionReasons.saa-ini-148:option:2: SQS FIFO is message queue, not orchestrator — does not coordinate the steps of a workflow.
optionReasons.saa-ini-148:option:3: The AWS Batch schedule batch computing jobs — does not orchestrate event-oriented state machines.

finalJustifications: Because Express Workflows were designed for high volume and short duration, with much higher rate limits and charge by number of executions and duration.
Because Express Workflows maintain the full run history by 90 days, taking into account the high volume audit requirement.
Because Express Workflows run within the infrastructure of SQS, inheriting the fee limits and the message cost of the rows.
Because Express Workflows are free even 1 billion monthly executions, and the Standard charges from the first execution of the flow.

optionReasons.saa-ini-293:option:0: The SQS use API of the AWS — the message layer JMS/AMQP the application would have to be rewritten.
optionReasons.saa-ini-293:option:1: The SNS is pub/sub with API of the AWS — would also require rewriting the message code.
optionReasons.saa-ini-293:option:2: The Kinesis is for data streaming — does not replace a message broker JMS/AMQP.

finalJustifications: Because Amazon MQ is an ActiveMQ and RabbitMQ-compatible managed broker — the application continues to use JMS/AMQP without changing the code.
Because Amazon MQ automatically converts calls JMS of the call application SQS, translating protocols in real time.
Because Amazon MQ is the serverless version of SNS, publishing the application's ActiveMQ topics without any stockbroker.
Because Amazon MQ removes broker: messages JMS/AMQP are delivered directly to the database of the migrated application.
